clue.text: Beetle to leave mark on sailor

parts.note: to leave a mark on skin is to scar it
AB, able seaman, is the crossword's usual sailor

explanation.surface: Someone sets out to leave a mark on a sailor, perhaps a tattoo or a bruise.
explanation.definitionFit: The scarab is the dung beetle held sacred in ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Wine with tea -almost Heaven!

parts.note: cha is a slang word for tea

indicators.note: almost means the word stops one letter short of its full length

parts.note: bliss, perfect happiness, is heaven

explanation.surface: A drinker finds wine taken with tea a near-heavenly experience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims the last S from BLISS, leaving BLIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Chablis is a dry white Burgundy, named after its French town.

clue.text: Investigate topless dress

indicators.note: topless says the word loses its top, which in a down clue is the first letter

parts.note: to probe is to investigate

explanation.surface: Someone is told to look into a revealing dress with no top.
explanation.definitionFit: A robe is a long loose gown, a kind of garment.

clue.text: 'Rock-a bye baby'? Be secure when rocking

indicators.note: rocking means the letters are shaken about and set in a new order

explanation.surface: A parent sings a lullaby, hoping the baby feels safe in the rocking cradle.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the nursery rhyme as one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A berceuse is a cradle song, a lullaby, and the rhyme is the best-known one in English.

clue.text: How some answer questions they don't know: a roundabout way?

definitions.text: How some answer questions they don't know
definitions.meaning: quiz contestants stuck for a reply get by with the word pass
a road that skirts a town goes round rather than through, sometimes via roundabouts

explanation.definitionFit: Quiz players dodge unknown questions by saying pass, and a bypass is a road routed around a town centre.

clue.text: Describing a lad by his love, possibly

indicators.note: possibly says these letters might be arranged some other way

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, so the letter O

explanation.surface: A lad is being described by his girlfriend, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' scrambles BY, HIS and O into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Boyish is an adjective for traits typical of a young male.

clue.text: Chap's unconscious and dies

parts.note: Peter is any man's name, a chap, here with possessive 's
someone knocked out is out cold

explanation.surface: A man falls unconscious and passes away.
explanation.definitionFit: To peter out is to dwindle and fade away to nothing, as in the expiring sense of dying.

clue.text: Not very well, in the main

definitions.text: Not very well, in the main

parts.words: Not very well, in the main
parts.note: reads as 'not well, by and large', but the main is the open sea, and feeling poorly there is a specific ailment

explanation.definitionFit: Being ill at sea from the ship's motion is nausea afloat; the main is an old term for the ocean.

clue.text: Fruit? First of costers rushed past, admitting mistake

indicators.note: First of says take only the opening letter of the word that follows
admitting means one piece lets another in, holding it within

parts.note: ran by means hurried past
to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: A costermonger, a London street fruit seller, notices someone rushing past his barrow.
explanation.walkthrough: Costers are costermongers, street sellers of fruit and vegetables in London, so the surface pictures a market stall; 'admitting' signals the container, and the question mark warns that the fruit is a particular berry.
explanation.definitionFit: The cranberry is a tart red berry grown in bogs.

clue.text: Fight to see result of gale warning?

definitions.meaning: a forecast of gales tells people that strong winds will arrive

explanation.definitionFit: Coming to blows means starting a physical scrap, and when a gale arrives, winds begin gusting hard.

clue.text: Salt water is running

definitions.meaning: the salty drops shed when crying
someone dashing along is moving fast, racing off

explanation.definitionFit: Tears are drops shed from the eyes, and someone who tears along is rushing at speed.

clue.text: Men i.e. agents sabotaged source of power

indicators.note: sabotaged means wrecked, so the letters are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Spies in a wartime plot wreck the plant that supplies a nation's power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sabotaged' rearranges the eleven letters of MEN, IE and AGENTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Boilers making pressurised vapour drove the pistons of locomotives and mills, the power plant of the industrial age.

clue.text: Spot what damages lawns

definitions.meaning: a small dark blemish on the skin
a burrowing animal that throws up heaps of earth across gardens

explanation.definitionFit: A mole is both a dark skin blemish and the small tunnelling mammal whose molehills ruin a lawn.

clue.text: China, perhaps, has a problem with crime

parts.note: a teaser is a puzzle, a tricky problem
vice is wickedness, criminal activity

explanation.surface: China, the country, is said to face a problem with crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country; with 'perhaps' it is porcelain, and the answer is one example of china.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of cups, saucers and pot for serving the brew is commonly made of porcelain.

clue.text: What luggage manufacturers do, for example

definitions.meaning: makers of suitcases try out their products for strength
an instance used as a precedent, especially in law

explanation.definitionFit: Makers try out each suitcase, and a lawsuit that sets a precedent is a model instance for later ones.

clue.text: Where sailor sits and brags, having got head of shark in net

parts.note: to crow is to boast

indicators.note: in places the shark's letter within the net
head of says take the first letter of the word after it

explanation.surface: A boastful fisherman has caught a shark in his net and sits bragging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head of' gives S from shark, which goes 'in' NET to make NEST.
explanation.definitionFit: The lookout platform near the top of a ship's mast is where a seaman keeps watch.

clue.text: It was often picked as a means of punishment

definitions.text: It was often picked as a means of punishment

parts.words: It was often picked as a means of punishment
parts.note: prisoners and workhouse inmates were set to unpicking old tarred rope as penal labour

explanation.definitionFit: Oakum is loose fibre teased from old rope, used for caulking ships; picking it was hard labour in Victorian prisons.

clue.text: Renovation needing tool brought up, in fact

indicators.note: in places the turned tool within the other word
brought up in a down clue means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a file is a tool for smoothing

explanation.surface: A renovation job, it turns out, needs the right tool to be fetched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' turns FILE into ELIF, which goes 'in' FACT.
explanation.definitionFit: A facelift is a cosmetic overhaul, figuratively a refurbishment of a building.

clue.text: Daring villain, British claim, snatching women

indicators.note: snatching means something is grabbed and taken away from the word

parts.note: to avow is to declare or claim

explanation.surface: A bold British rogue makes a claim and runs off with women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snatching' removes W from AVOW, leaving AVO.
explanation.definitionFit: A bravo is a hired desperado or bandit, the bold cut-throat of old romance.

clue.text: Pleasantness and friendship enveloping bridge opponents

indicators.note: enveloping means the first word wraps around the second

parts.note: amity is friendship
in bridge East and North sit on opposing sides, so E and N

explanation.surface: Friendly relations envelop the players across the card table.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge North and South partner against East and West, so E and N are opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: An amenity is an agreeable feature, and the word also means agreeableness itself.

clue.text: Piano skill is shown by a new champion

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
art is skill

explanation.surface: A pianist's skill is displayed by a newcomer.
explanation.definitionFit: A partisan is a committed supporter, one who champions a cause.

clue.text: Food terminology found in South Africa

parts.note: usage is the way words are used

explanation.surface: A word for a dish is part of the local vocabulary in South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' only links the pieces: SA stands first, then USAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sausage is minced meat in a skin, a staple of the braai grill.

clue.text: Cricket official more annoyed about century?

indicators.note: about means the first word goes around the second

parts.note: sorer means more irritated
C is a hundred in Roman numerals, a century

explanation.surface: An umpire grows crosser over a batsman's hundred.
explanation.walkthrough: A century in cricket is a hundred runs.
explanation.definitionFit: The scorer records runs and wickets in the scorebook at a cricket match.

clue.text: Everyone claims not to know it (so pretence is organised)

definitions.text: Everyone claims not to know it

indicators.note: organised says these letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Everybody pretends to be ignorant of the matter, and the pretence is well arranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Something widely known yet officially unacknowledged is hush-hush in name only.

clue.text: File under Japanese icon', primarily

indicators.note: primarily says take the opening letter of each word

explanation.surface: A librarian is told to shelve something under a Japanese symbol.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letters of File, Under, Japanese, Icon spell the answer, which is itself a Japanese icon.
explanation.definitionFit: The snow-capped volcano is Japan's national symbol.

clue.text: Goddess or male god?

parts.note: he is a male pronoun
Ra is the Egyptian sun god

explanation.surface: A deity's sex is in question: goddess or god?
explanation.definitionFit: Hera was queen of the Olympian deities, wife of Zeus.

clue.text: Birds suddenly move into Kent?

indicators.note: into means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Kent is in south-east England, SE
to nip is to dart quickly

explanation.surface: Some birds suddenly fly into the county of Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in the South East of England, abbreviated SE. The plural of the bird is unchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: Snipe are long-billed wading birds, and the plural form is the same as the singular.

clue.text: Speak again about showing ability to read (though not at first)

parts.note: re means about, concerning

indicators.note: not at first says drop the opening letter

parts.note: literate means able to read

explanation.surface: A tutor reports on a pupil now showing reading ability, though not at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not at first' drops the L from LITERATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To reiterate is to repeat something said.

clue.text: Some boys terrorise a reserved lad?

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A few boys bully a shy, quiet lad.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone close as a clam, who keeps their thoughts shut away, is called this shellfish.

clue.text: Old Father and Mother going for a spin in the Sun

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the others

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: going for a spin means the word turns around, reading backwards

parts.note: ma is mother

explanation.surface: An old father and mother take a drive in the sunshine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going for a spin' turns MA into AM, which goes 'in' THE plus S.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Father Thames is the traditional personification of London's river.
